status: Detailed standalone open-air amphitheater asset rebuilt from official venue envelope and Purdue-published architectural/program facts; placement/orientation and height remain estimated pending independent grade.

sources.provider: Purdue University campus building footprint service (ArcGIS FeatureServer)
sources.geometry_use: Mapped outdoor venue envelope; not a surveyed stage wall footprint.

sources.provider: Purdue Arboretum, official Purdue University page
uses: 56 ft stage front, 34 ft back, 46 ft depth

architectural description: Stonehenge-inspired stelae back/side walls; yellow French-glass and black epoxy-resin infill; undulating suspended concrete ceiling on stainless-steel cables from a steel tripod; roof does not touch stage sides

sources.provider: Purdue Arboretum official page photograph, source image EXIF metadata
sources.use: Visual reference for canopy silhouette, tripod supports, cable fan, stone stelae, amber inserts, stage platform, and open grassy setting; image does not provide georeferenced orientation.

coordinate_system.project_frame: X east, Y north, Z up; meters; local approximate conversion
coordinate_system.method: Project each official GIS ring coordinate into the project local approximation before testing model vertex locations.

modeled_stage_plan_m.evidence: Direct conversion of Purdue-published dimensions: 56 ft, 34 ft, 46 ft.

source_polygon_comparison.method: Ray-cast point-in-polygon on every mesh vertex after projecting the official ring into project local coordinates.
source_polygon_comparison.result: All structural and terrain vertices fall inside the official venue envelope polygon. This validates envelope containment, not that the mapped polygon is a surveyed stage-wall outline.

measurements.position_status: Estimated. The stage is placed near the west quarter of the official mapped venue envelope; this internal placement is not independently georeferenced.
measurements.orientation_status: Estimated east-facing orientation; no georeferenced plan, surveyed stage footprint, or photo camera position is available to establish bearing.
measurements.height_status: Unverified estimate. The tripod apex is modeled at 12.35 m and the mast reaches 13.15 m; no official elevation or surveyed height was found.
measurements.audience_landscape_status: A gently rising grass fan suggests the documented grassy knoll; detailed terrain contours and capacity seating are not modeled or surveyed.

geometry_edits: Rebuilt the simple prototype as a detailed amphitheater mesh while preserving the manifest asset ID, existing object name, collection, scene, one-object library contract, campus coordinate frame and linked asset path.
Modeled an open trapezoidal stage using the Purdue-published 56 ft front, 34 ft rear and 46 ft depth dimensions.

Replaced solid side/back walls with sculpted, poly-cylindrical concrete stelae and alternating yellow/amber glass and black resin panels; the stage remains open at the performance front and the canopy floats above the side walls.

Modeled an undulating, thin concrete cloud canopy with 32 radial suspension cables, a three-leg weathering-steel tripod, low stone podium walls, stage apron steps, a discreet backstage recess, and a gently rising grass audience knoll.

Added ten portable procedural materials for stage concrete, stelae, amber glass, epoxy resin, weathering steel, canopy concrete, limestone, grass, apron and backstage recess; no external image path or add-on is required.

validation.fresh_open: Stable library reopened in Blender 5.2.3 LTS after copying from the validated candidate.
validation.preview: preview_detail.png (front elevation perspective after tripod proportion refinement)

uncertainties: The official GIS feature is a mapped venue envelope rather than a stage wall survey; internal stage placement and bearing remain estimates.

Purdue sources do not publish height, elevation contours, tripod dimensions, canopy measurements, stela spacing, or an architectural plan; those features are modeled from the official qualitative description and an official 2013 photograph.
The lawn fan is schematic and does not represent surveyed hill contours or seating capacity.
Independent quality grading remains pending; parent coordinator will review this stable asset.
